Database search

Source: R/frns2.R
dbsrch.Rd

What a match found by trawling a database is worth. np is the bound of the second National Research Council report: the match probability times the number of profiles searched. any is the exact chance of at least one chance match among that many unrelated profiles, never above np. post takes the other view (Balding and Donnelly): everyone else in the database was excluded, so among pop possible sources with equal prior the matching person's probability of being the source goes up, not down. See proof("dbsrch").

Usage

dbsrch(mp, n, pop = NULL)

Arguments

mp

The profile match probability: one number above 0 and at most 1.

n

The number of profiles searched, the match included.

pop

NULL, or the number of possible sources, at least n.

Value

A named numeric vector: np, any and, when pop is given, post.

References

Balding, D. J. and Donnelly, P. (1996). Evaluating DNA profile evidence when the suspect is identified through a database search. Journal of Forensic Sciences, 41(4), 603-607. doi:10.1520/JFS13961J

Examples

dbsrch(mp = 1e-9, n = 5e6, pop = 3e7)
#>          np         any        post 
#> 0.005000000 0.004987521 0.975609756
